purpose.value: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 625 °C for 3 h (and across the full aging matrix).

key_findings.value: 15Al aged at 625 °C for 3 h gave 889.9 ± 4.3 HV; at 625 °C and 650 °C the hardness of the 15Al alloy stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy the 625 °C aging series was essentially time-independent: 852.8 ± 24.6 HV (1 h), 889.9 ± 4.3 HV (3 h), 887.2 ± 14.1 HV (6 h) and 888.2 ± 6.6 HV (10 h) (Table 2), i.e. the 15Al hardness at 625 °C (and 650 °C) remained stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time (b0028, b0037).

At 600 °C and above (including 625 °C), the α matrix of the 15Al alloy almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h of aging, and abundant fine BCC and FCC precipitates were observed within the β-Mn (b0052).
The peak Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy (965.6 HV) was achieved at 600 °C for 6 h, not at the 625 °C/3 h condition of this sample (b0028, b0037, b0055).
